name: OpenCode
verdict: A free MIT coding agent for the terminal, desktop, and a local web UI; the models are your own bill, or a $10 Go plan with a separate cap per model.
pros: The agent itself is MIT licensed
Terminal, desktop app, and a local web UI
Go is optional if you already have a provider
cons: Go limits are a dollar cap per model, not one shared pool
A Go workspace cannot invite members
pricingNote: Checked 2026-10-15. opencode.ai/go lists Go at $10/month and Go Plus at $40/month. opencode.ai/docs/go says Go is optional, a Go workspace cannot invite members, and each model has its own monthly dollar limit, with 20% of that limit in any 5 hours and 50% in a week. Those per-model amounts are not one pool, so they are not collapsed into a single figure here. The MIT license is at github.com/anomalyco/opencode. Zen, on opencode.ai/zen, is pay as you go: a $20 starting balance plus a $1.23 card fee, and another $20 when the balance reaches $5. The v2 billing docs list Console credit packs of $10, $50, and $100 with a processing fee of 4.6% + $0.31, and no seat fee. Usage through your own provider is billed by that provider.
